sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy is compounding on rising middle-class consumption and e-commerce penetration, making local tech platforms structurally less sensitive to US rate cycles.
Government-led digital infrastructure and financial inclusion mandates (QRIS, e-KYC, fintech licensing) are creating durable moats for domestic payment and marketplace players.
Regional divergence persists: US tech valuations face repricing risk from AI capex fatigue, while ASEAN tech trades on local demand, offering a hedge for Indonesia-focused portfolios.
sectors.ai: Buy the Indonesia tech dip selectively: local names (BELI, IRSX, WGSH, BUKA) are decoupling from US weakness on domestic consumption and digital-payment adoption, while US-listed peers drag the aggregate. Rotate into high-beta local winners with earnings momentum; avoid US-exposed tech until Fed signals shift.

Regulatory tailwinds for sharia-compliant and micro-lending products are creating durable niches, lifting BGTG, BBLD, and TRJA as domestic liquidity rotates into specialized lenders.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy-transition policy, including the RUPTL and carbon trading, is structurally accelerating domestic renewables demand, favoring local champions like ESSA and CSAP over US-listed peers.
Captive power and industrial decarbonization (BRPT, TPIA) are durable growth drivers as manufacturing shifts to green inputs, insulating these names from global rate volatility.
Geothermal and bioenergy (BREN, CDIA) benefit from baseload reliability and government subsidies, creating a structural premium over intermittent solar (SEDG) in Southeast Asia.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesian renewables, led by ESSA and CSAP, as domestic momentum (+0.80%) outpaces US weakness; the NORMAL signal supports selective accumulation. Favor names with captive feedstock (ESSA, BRPT) and grid-expansion exposure (CDIA, EIX) over pure-play solar (SEDG). Trim TPIA on valuation, but hold BREN for long-term geothermal optionality.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Domestic consumption resilience drives outsized gains in small/mid-cap FMCG names, as local purchasing power remains robust despite global headwinds.
Pricing power and distribution reach separate winners from laggards, favoring companies with strong brand equity and rural penetration.
US-linked FMCG underperformance signals a structural shift toward local champions, as investors prioritize domestic demand over export-oriented plays.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in high-momentum names (KKES, COCO, ENZO) as local consumer demand stays resilient, but trim exposure to US-linked FMCG laggards. Focus on domestic staples with strong distribution and pricing power; expect continued rotation into small/mid-cap winners. Maintain normal risk, add on dips.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's universal health coverage (JKN) expansion continues to drive volume growth for hospital chains and pharmaceutical distributors, insulating them from global macro swings.

Regulatory support for local vaccine and generic drug manufacturing (e.g., NOVN, DKHH) is accelerating import substitution, creating structural margin expansion opportunities.

Rotate into NOVN for vaccine upside. Maintain neutral US exposure; MRNA/CVS rallies are sentiment-driven, not structural.
